successors.name: Qin (state)
successors.text: Ba in the Sichuan basin: Chongqing and eastern Sichuan with Langzhong, after Chu pushed Ba west

ledger.x: 703 BC: Ba enters the record in the Hubei Han valley.
About 500 BC (page silent on the year): Chu pushes Ba out of the Hubei core.
About 500 BC (page silent on the year): Ba is established in the Sichuan basin.
316 BC: the Ba state ends as a Qin commandery.

wars.name: Ba and Chu attack on Deng
wars.outcome: A joint Chu-Ba operation against Deng in 703 BC, Ba's first definite appearance; the page gives no territorial result (Chu annexed Deng later, see the Chu dossier).

wars.name: Revolt of the Ba mercenaries at Chu
wars.outcome: Ba mercenaries serving Chu 'rebelled and besieged the Chu capital' in 676 or 675 BC; no territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Qin conquest of Shu and Ba
wars.outcome: Qin took Shu and then Ba in 316 and made Ba a commandery.

certainty.note: No Ba boundary is documented; capitals only.
